digest.component_or_area: review-bot comment-added event routing and eligibility gating
propositions: A `recheck-review` Gerrit comment token triggers re-review of the current patchset only when the bot's latest LLM-Review vote on that revision is NOT a real finding BLOCK, refusing explicitly if it is a finding and harmonizing with ticket 0347's per-revision retry budget.

The eligibility precheck reads the bot's authoritative LLM-Review vote message tag from Gerrit state (via GET /a/changes/{id}/messages), strips trailing `(merge-change, N integrated commit(s))` suffix, and classifies the stem to exclude only `[LLM-Review: BLOCK — finding]` variants; all other states (coverage-gap sub-reasons, retries-exhausted escalation, PASS, unparseable) are eligible.

A `recheck-review` comment accepted for re-review resets the 0347 attempts budget, enqueues via `_rebar_force`, posts a vote-free reply message (no `labels` key in the Gerrit REST body), and emits `RETRIGGER_ACCEPTED`; a refused comment posts a vote-free reply explaining the finding must be fixed and emits `RETRIGGER_REFUSED`.

The contributor surface adds `event = comment-added` to `infra/gerrit/webhooks.config`; app.py worker routes `comment-added` events to retrigger.handle_comment_added() which validates token match, ignores bot-authored comments, and enforces the eligibility gate before any state change.

The `/rerun` operator endpoint is harmonized to reset the 0347 attempts budget before enqueueing, maintaining unrestricted operator semantics while the contributor comment path enforces the finding refusal security property.

Gerrit client gains two REST helpers: `get_change_messages(change_id)` (GET /a/changes/{id}/messages) and `post_comment(change_id, revision, message)` (POST /a/changes/{id}/revisions/{rev}/review with message-only JSON body).
